name: shiftwork_draft
title: Shift work: draft
description: Shift-work draft: turn tickets into a new job — a checkpoint that validates against the checkpoint schema, plus one brief file per ticket — so step 1 of the shift-work loop is not typed by hand. Call it once, when a job's tickets are settled and before the first shiftwork_clock_in; it never edits a job in progress (that is the planner's edit, or shiftwork_clock_out's `follow_ups`), and work_plan is the read-only answer when all you want is the batches. Every ticket needs a non-empty `id`, `title`, `role`, `verify`, `data_shape` (the types, fields, files or messages the unit produces or consumes — a ticket without one is not ready to execute) and `brief`; the first missing one is refused by name. The graph is work_plan's: its refusals come back verbatim, `batches` and `width` are its answer, and `cursor` is the first ready unit, the one shiftwork_clock_out would pick. With job.roles declared, a ticket role it does not name is refused. Each ticket becomes a `todo` unit with brief_path <briefs_dir>/<id>.md; any other ticket key (touches, reviews, irreversible, ...) is copied onto the unit, and the composed document must pass the checkpoint schema and shiftwork_plan's graph checks, or the schema's sentence is the refusal. `write` is false by default: the document and every brief's text come back and nothing is touched. With `write: true` the briefs and then the checkpoint are written by temp file + rename under <checkpoint>.lock; an existing checkpoint, or an existing brief with other bytes, is refused before anything is written, and a failure part-way names what landed in `written`. It never runs git, never runs `verify` and never reads the working tree: `repo` is taken as given. Refusals are {"result": "error", "reason"}, never exceptions.

job.title: Job
job.description: The checkpoint's `job` object, copied as given: id, goal, done_definition, constraints, and optional roles, budget or agreements.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.description: One per unit, in plan order. Keys other than the six required ones, depends_on and priority are copied onto the unit and judged by the checkpoint schema.

id.description: The unit id, and the brief's file name: no /, \ or :, no leading dot.

role.description: planner, implementer or reviewer; with job.roles declared, one of its keys.

depends_on.description: Ticket ids it waits for; absent means none.

verify.description: The command that proves the unit done.

data_shape.description: The types, fields, files or messages the unit produces or consumes.

brief.description: The brief's body, written under the heading; CRLF becomes LF.

priority.description: work_plan's tie-break inside a batch (higher first); used for the cursor, not stored on the unit.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: state.repo as given: {branch, head_sha, dirty}. Never read from git.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Where the checkpoint is written with write: true, absolute or relative to the server's working directory; default .shiftwork/checkpoint.json.

briefs_dir.title: Briefs Dir
briefs_dir.description: Directory of the brief files, also the prefix of every brief_path; default .shiftwork/briefs.

handoff.title: Handoff
handoff.description: Optional do_not, open_questions and notes for the checkpoint's handoff; next_action is always written as `Read <cursor brief> and clock in <cursor>.`

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: {path, role} entries (spec, plan) appended to state.artifacts after one brief entry per unit.

write.title: Write
write.description: true writes the briefs and the checkpoint; false or absent is a dry run that touches nothing.

result.description: `draft` on success; `error` with `reason` for the first refusal.

reason.description: The refusal sentence, when result is `error`.

checkpoint.description: The composed checkpoint document, valid against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

cursor.description: plan.cursor: the first unit of the first batch.

batches.description: work_plan's batches over the tickets, priorities included.

briefs.description: One per unit: its id, its brief_path, and `bytes`, the file's full UTF-8 text.

written.description: Paths written by this call, briefs first and the checkpoint last; [] on a dry run, and on a write-side refusal the paths that landed before it.
